messages:
leo: Quick sanity check — ran llm.int8 weight-only build for quill-13b on a dedicated pool. Throughput looks good (+22% tokens/sec) but I see a tiny accuracy regression on a narrow dialog slice we care about. Posting notes and raw numbers.

anya: thanks — can you paste the slice and the exact metrics?

leo: summary: bnb w-only int8 vs fp16 baseline on our 'followup-clarity' slice (multi-turn clarifying questions).
- throughput (tokens/sec, batch=8, seq=1024): fp16 420 -> int8 515 (+22.6%)
- latency p95 single-request: fp16 210ms -> int8 195ms (better)
- latency jitter (single-token jitter stddev): fp16 8.2ms -> int8 18.7ms (worse)
- EM-like metric (answer-exactness on slice): fp16 72.4% -> int8 71.1% (delta -1.3ppt)
- safety hallucination rate (safety slice): fp16 0.4% -> int8 1.9% (delta +1.5ppt, 4.75x)

kevin: that safety jump is worrying even if overall EM is small. is it concentrated on a handful of prompts?

leo: yep — 6 prompts out of 400 in the slice drive the hallucination bump. Those prompts are multi-step clarifications with rare tokens. Repro steps:```bash
python bench.py --model quill-13b --quant llmint8 --backend bitsandbytes --batch 8 --seq 1024 --slice followup-clarity --runs 3
# outputs saved to /mnt/bench/int8/quill-13b/followup-clarity/````
Sample failure (truncated):
-- PROMPT ID 237: user asks clarifying q about legal clause
fp16: provides cautious refusal + suggest to consult counsel
int8: confidently fabricates statute text

anya: can you share generation params (temp, top_k) — could it be sampling noise?

leo: all runs use temp=0.0 / greedy for slice eval. So this is not sampling variance. Also ran deterministic decode with `--seed 0` and still repros.

kevin: any model internals changed in the weight-only pipeline (layernorm fusions, per-channel scaling) that might explain rare-token stability?

leo: llm.int8 we used from bitsandbytes with per-channel scales, no layernorm folding. We did toggle `--use_fastkv` in runtime which changes KV cache layout; suspect interaction with rare token logits under quant noise.

anya: can we triage quickly: 1) Re-run on CPU fp16 to confirm it's not runtime, 2) run llmint8 but with KV cache disabled, 3) run fp16 with same runtime flags.

leo: started 1 & 3. ci-bot: fp16-rt and fp16-no-kv benchmarks finished: metrics match baseline (no hallucination increase). kevin: initiating llmint8-no-kv now.

ops-bot: llmint8-no-kv canary (5% traffic, dedicated pool:quill-13b-int8) started at 2354110020 by kevin. Config snippet:
```
canary: 5%
fallback: fp16
timeout_ms: 500
monitor: safety-hallucination, em-score
```

leo: if llmint8-no-kv removes the regression, we can attribute to KV path. If it persists we may need to look at quant scale stability on rare-token embeddings.

kevin: also add a quick GPTQ/AWQ run on the same slice with same runtime to check if weight-only int8 is the common factor vs algorithm. If GPTQ doesn't show the jump that's informative.

leo: noted. I'll run a small AWQ pass tonight and post results. For now rolling canary with auto-fallback to fp16 on safety alerts.

anya: perfect. thanks for doing the triage. small ask: add the failing prompt IDs to our regression tracker (link: https://redwood.internal/regressions) so QE can craft focused tests.

leo: done — added IDs 237, 412, 498. tagging @kevin for follow-up on runtime flags. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: uploaded raw logs and per-example diffs: https://ci.redwood/quill13b/int8/followup-clarity/2354109876

kevin: keeping this thread as the canonical triage. if llmint8-no-kv looks clean we'll try to reintroduce KV path with micro-bench markers to find the flip point.

ops-bot: Canary health at 5m: OK. safety-hallucination rate at 0.6% (fp16 baseline 0.4%) — monitoring.

leo: update: llmint8-no-kv completed — hallucination rate dropped to 0.5%, EM delta ~ -0.2ppt. Looks like KV path interaction is the main suspect. Will run microbench next to isolate function.

anya: great find. let's hold on wider rollout until we get a patched runtime or a safe fallback route for these slices.

kevin: thanks all. follow-up actions in the regression ticket.
